heroSection.description: A Java-focused Full-Stack Engineer specializing in high-performance backends and clean, maintainable frontends. I build software that solves real problems without the fluff.

about.endingLine: Engineered for long-term stability and human readability under change.

segments.title: How I Think
segments.label: Clarity
segments.text: I focus on writing code that is easy to understand and hard to break. I value clear logic and correctness over clever shortcuts, so the software I build remains reliable as it grows.

segments.title: How I Build
segments.label: Foundations
segments.text: Java and Spring Boot for backend, React and Next.js for frontend, Terraform and Ansible for the  that makes it all run in production. I don't stop at 'runs locally.'

segments.title: How I Learn
segments.label: Iteration
segments.text: I learn by building, breaking, and fixing with understanding — not by memorising patterns. Every project in this portfolio was deliberately overengineered to force me into problems I had never solved before.

segments.title: Where I'm Going
segments.label: Growth
segments.text: Deepening system design intuition, distributed systems patterns, and the gap between 'it works on my machine' and 'it works under load at 3am on a Tuesday.' That's the interesting part.

projects.title: Hermes
projects.tagline: Production-grade real-time encrypted chat — private messaging, group chats, and a two-VM Kubernetes cluster on GCP to run it all.
projects.description: Hermes is a full-stack, end-to-end encrypted real-time messaging platform supporting private and group chat, deployed on a self-managed k3s Kubernetes cluster on GCP — provisioned from zero via Terraform and Ansible. The server never sees plaintext private message content. The CI/CD pipeline catches it before you do.
highlights: End-to-end encrypted messaging using WebCrypto, ECDH P-256, and AES-GCM. Server never sees plaintext messages.
Self-managed k3s cluster on GCP provisioned with Terraform and configured through Ansible automation.
GitHub Actions CI/CD with security scanning, Docker builds, Kubernetes rollouts, and observability monitoring.

projects.title: Pokeverse
projects.tagline: A real-time multiplayer game platform built to host multiple interactive games under a shared infrastructure — so you only solve auth, rooms, and WebSockets once.
projects.description: Pokeverse centralises the solved problems every multiplayer game re-invents — authentication, room lifecycle, real-time event routing, chat, and state management — into a reusable platform backend. Individual game types plug in as modules. A Pokémon Quiz demonstrates it in both single-player and multiplayer modes using the shared infrastructure.
highlights: Reusable multiplayer platform handling authentication, rooms, messaging, persistence, and real-time event routing.
PostgreSQL stores durable game data while Redis powers low-latency active session management.
Pokémon Quiz module supports single-player and multiplayer gameplay with live scoring and WebSocket updates.

projects.title: Calculate
projects.tagline: A scientific expression evaluator built with compiler techniques — because calling eval() is cheating.
projects.description: A scientific expression evaluator built from scratch using classic compiler techniques — tokenisation, implicit multiplication injection, Shunting-Yard postfix conversion, and stack-based evaluation. Supports 50+ mathematical functions and 70+ operators with zero external math dependencies. Comes with a Medium article explaining how it works, because the implementation alone is only half the point.
highlights: Built from scratch using tokenization, Shunting-Yard conversion, and stack-based postfix evaluation.
Supports 50+ functions and 70+ operators without relying on external math libraries.
Includes 100+ tests and a published Medium article explaining implementation decisions.

data.label: JavaScript
data.description: Dynamic, event-driven language powering the web; flexible but prone to runtime errors without strong constraints.

data.label: TypeScript
data.description: Statically typed superset of JavaScript. Dominant language across Hermes frontend, Pokeverse frontend, and the portfolio — 51%, 82%, and 94% of those repos respectively.

data.label: Java
data.description: Primary language for all backend work. Spring Boot 3.3.4 in Hermes, Spring Boot 3.5.5 in Pokeverse — production-grade, not tutorial-grade.

data.label: Python
data.description: 100% of the Calculate project — 600+ lines, 100+ test cases, proper packaging with pyproject.toml. Used when Java would be overkill.

data.label: React
data.description: Component-based UI library powering Hermes (React 18), Pokeverse (React 19.1.0), and the portfolio (React 19.1.0). Multiple production frontends, not just hello-world.

data.label: Next.js
data.description: React framework providing routing, SSR, and production-grade tooling. Live on Vercel for the portfolio; Pokeverse frontend runs Next.js 15.5.3.

data.label: Tailwind CSS
data.description: Utility-first CSS framework enforcing design consistency. Tailwind 4 in Pokeverse and the portfolio — current-gen, not the tutorial version.

data.label: Spring Boot
data.description: Opinionated Java framework for production-ready backend services. Two separate projects: 3.3.4 in Hermes, 3.5.5 in Pokeverse. WebSocket, Security, JPA, OAuth2 — the whole stack.

data.label: PostgreSQL
data.description: PostgreSQL 17 with Flyway-managed schema versioning in Pokeverse. Chosen over MySQL here for its stronger constraint system and richer query capabilities.

data.label: MySQL
data.description: MySQL 8 with JPA/Hibernate in Hermes. Schema covers users, roles, messages, groups, and file metadata. Nightly backup CronJob in Kubernetes because data loss is not a feature.

data.label: Redis
data.description: Redis 7 in both projects — image caching, per-user sliding window rate limiting, pub-sub, and E2EE public key distribution in Hermes; low-latency active game session state in Pokeverse.

data.label: Docker
data.description: Multi-stage builds, non-root users, minimal base images in Hermes. Docker Compose for local dev. The kind of Dockerfile hygiene that makes security reviewers nod.

data.label: Kubernetes
data.description: k3s on GCP in Hermes — Deployments, StatefulSets, Ingress, NetworkPolicies, HPA, CronJob, ConfigMaps, Secrets, cert-manager. Default-deny NetworkPolicies. Two-VM cluster, managed from scratch.

data.label: Terraform
data.description: GCP provider in Hermes — VPC, subnet, firewall rules, two compute instances. HCL is 1.7% of the Hermes repo; it provisions 100% of the infrastructure.

data.label: Ansible
data.description: Hermes playbooks: bootstrap, kubernetes, deploy-k8s, monitoring, and security. Automates everything from package installation to UFW hardening to k3s cluster formation.

data.label: GitHub Actions
data.description: Full CI/CD pipeline in Hermes: unit tests → Trivy scan (images + IaC) → SHA-tagged multi-stage Docker build → push to Docker Hub → kubectl rollout → smoke test. Every step earns its place.

data.label: Prometheus
data.description: Scrapes /actuator/prometheus in Hermes. Feeds Grafana dashboards covering JVM heap/GC, HTTP latency percentiles, WebSocket connections, Redis hit/miss, MySQL pool, and HPA replica count.

data.label: Grafana
data.description: Deployed via Ansible in Hermes. Dashboards cover the full operational picture — not just 'is it up', but 'is it healthy under load.'

data.label: Git
data.description: Distributed version control system enabling collaboration, history tracking, and safe iteration.

data.label: JWT
data.description: Stateless token format for authentication. Dual-token (access + refresh) in Pokeverse; stateless in Hermes. Cookie-based storage. Filter chain integration — not bolted on as an afterthought.

data.label: OAuth 2.0
data.description: Google OAuth2 social login in both Hermes and Pokeverse. Hermes supports hybrid email/password + OAuth2. Pokeverse centralises it as a platform service shared across game modules.

footer.note: Everything's open source. Take it, build better.
